# R3.6 — Assembly emitter adjudication (BL-10 / DF-S1.9-2 residual)

**Ticket:** `docs/tickets/142_R3.6__assembly-emitter-adjudication.md`
(seq 6 of 11, Round 3, manifest row 142). **Requirement ids:**
`DF-S1.9-2`, `BL-10`; `R-2.1.4`, `R-2.1.3`; ADR-0358 (new), CF-492
(new register row). **Base:** `svitali/harnessharness-r3.5` — the
stacked R3.5 tip (operator merges; mergePolicy: OPERATOR). **Layer:**
fixture-verified — offline/hermetic only; no staging/live claims, no
credentials, no production mutations.

## What

Discharges **DF-S1.9-2**'s last residual — the emitter-vs-exemption
adjudication for the eleven diagnostic codes no document path emits
today — and closes **BL-10**. Every code in the AC-CC-11 INDEX is now
adjudicated: each either gained a real emitter or a permanent ruling
whose reason names the owning producer **and** the concrete condition
that would re-open it. Map totals unchanged: 36 `F` / 49 `X` / 9 `U` /
1 `N` over 95.

**1. `C-LINK-8` / `C-LINK-9` gained real emitters (`U` → `X`).**
`CompileError` gained the `LinkError{diagnostics}` carriage on the two
standalone link-stage variants — `link` mints `C-LINK-8` at the
`resolve_chain` ambiguous-selector tie and `C-LINK-9` at the
dialect-narrowing check; `family::check_dialect_transform` mints
`C-LINK-9` under compiler provenance; `hh-compile` preserves
`diagnostics` in the JSON error path; `hh-embed`'s
`lab.assembly.compile` surfaces `compile_diagnostics`;
`hh-lab` stage-6b reports a carried row verbatim and still spells the
code on diagnostics-empty refusals. The rows are `X`, not `F`: the
corpus driver lives in `hh-assembly` and cannot depend upward on
`hh-compiler`, so the fixture-emitted class is structurally
unreachable — emission is pinned by `hh-compiler`/`hh-lab` batteries
that fail if the mint or the carriage is removed.

**2. `C-REF-2` / `C-REF-3` re-classified `X` → `U` — honestly.**
An existing error *type* is not emission of the code: `C-REF-3` is
minted by registry publish/admission, never a document stage;
`C-REF-2`'s ambiguity arm exists in `resolve` but the newest-match
selection rule makes it unproducible from a valid document. Both
reasons now name the owner and the re-open precondition.

**3. Seven `U` rulings with named owners + re-open preconditions.**
`C-PROF-3` (experiment-plane `ExperimentRefusal`), `C-LCD-1` (the
closed `EdgeKind` set has no host edge kind — the validate:7 scan is
armed but unreachable), `C-LOC-1`/`C-TRUST-1` (instantiate
`BindFailure`/`BindReason` — bind events, not document diagnostics),
`C-RES-1` (`verify_resume` verdict → `EmbedError::DefinitionChanged`),
`C-SEAL-1` (compiler stage-5 seal self-check — defect-gated; the
§3.3.8 stage-set gap is **CF-492**), `C-CLASS-7` (registry-admission
dialect-compatibility refusal).

**4. Build memory.** DF-S1.9-2 `DONE` (dated); BL-10 `closed`;
R-2.1.4 `PARTIAL → MET`; ADR-0358 + a dated Re-check appended to
ADR-0350 (append-only — the corpus ruling is not reopened);
`research/registers/conflicts.md` CF-492; `docs/adr/README.md`
regenerated via `adr-index.sh`.

## Finding for the operator

**CF-492** — §3.3.8's closed `Stage` set (`desugar`, `compose`,
`resolve`, `validate:1–7`, `link`, `lower`, `instantiate`, `resume`)
has no `seal` spelling for `C-SEAL-1`'s producer (the compiler's
stage-5 re-encode self-check). Interim convention: the producing check
reports under `validate:6b`. The spec process owns the ruling — add
`seal` to the closed set or re-home the code.
